result:
**Verdict: PASS for DG6 candidate `sha256:32e41b55…76b5`, with no new findings.** All four open findings verify CLOSED_VERIFIED: F-DG6-960, F-DG6-970 and F-DG6-980 (Medium; the same history-channel defect) and F-DG6-971 (Low).

**Candidate identity**
- The ID matched (2773 files) at the start and the end on the complete, non-shallow tree, and over the source commit `f56f1b3d2`.
- The product tree equals `a0cf22bba`.
- HEAD moved twice during my run, when the other two reviewers' runs were auto-committed. Neither commit touches anything outside `docs/delivery`, and I did not open their records.

**The four open findings**
- **F-DG6-980 (my own) and F-DG6-960 (domain):** the round-2 probes now pass. A withheld earlier answer is no longer sent to the model, and no new answer re-serves its text.
- **F-DG6-970 (code-security):** its probe still fails, as the repair's handback said it would. I checked why: when there is no history, the probe's own fake model answers with a fixed text that names the revoked record. The request the product sends holds no revoked title, fact or ID, so I accepted that explanation.
- **F-DG6-971:** the code-security probe fails in its own setup, because the database rule it tries to drop no longer exists. My own version passes: an old (pre-0128) suggestion can now be taken to a draft. A context still cannot be added to it later, and a new row without one is still refused.
- **Reverting the fix brings the defects back.** With the history fix removed (mutant M1), my round-2 probe reproduces the original defect again. With migration 0129 removed (mutant M2), the old suggestion is refused again (422).

**My round-3 probe of the repair (8/8 pass)**
- The inherited context carries through more than six turns, past the history window.
- A permission revoked while the model call is in flight still hides the new answer.
- Suggestions inherit the answer's context and cannot be taken to a draft after a revocation.
- The 1,000-key limit holds exactly: 50 answers × 20 records with nothing dropped, and a 51st turn is refused.
- Restoring a permission makes the earlier answer visible to the model again.
- Run 1 failed on one case because of my own probe's setup (the test user lacked a grant). I fixed the probe, not the product, and I report both runs.
- One gap remains, and the repair already discloses it. Answers stored between migrations 0128 and 0129 did not record what they inherited, so after a revocation they stay readable. I don't count it as a defect: such rows exist only where the unreleased intermediate build ran, and nothing from DG6 has shipped.

**Full test run**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Static (7 checks) | All exit 0; the API contract has 932 operations |
| Unit, Node 22 and 24, both locale settings | All exit 0 |
| Integration, twice | 441/441 files and 4,366 tests each time; migrations 0001–0129 applied |
| tests/qa alone | 45 files, 437 tests pass |
| Product e2e, both locale settings | 556 passed, 2 skipped by design |
| Root acceptance e2e, both locale settings | 288 passed, 18 declared skips |
| Network capture during e2e | Every connection went to loopback |
| Demo e2e | 10/10, twice |
| Accessibility (axe) | 0 serious or critical issues |
| Extra probes | 360/390 px and 200 % text, read-only auditor pass, script injection shown as text, keyboard walkthrough, token sequences, Arabic export literals, worker burst (0 duplicates): all pass |
| Load and async export | Within the provisional targets on one sandbox host, not Mobily capacity |
| Gate validators | All PASS |

**Things I could not run or that behaved differently**
- `/opt/node22` is version 22.22.0, not the 22.22.2 the assignment names; I recorded what I ran.
- The kernel killed one process for lack of memory while my second clone was building. The build still exited 0 and every later run completed.
- The export-proof script exits 1 on a known gap in the load dataset (LOAD-T20 has no second same-scope user). The register notes already disclose it, and it is not a speed or access failure.
- The sandbox refused my sweep of leftover test files in my private temp folder. That folder is removed when the run ends, and my disposable clones are already deleted.
- After I wrote my record, `validate.mjs --stage DG6` on the main repository still lists DG6 requirements as unchecked by the reviewers. That is expected: my records sit in my run's private staging copy until the runner copies them back.

**D-229 and D-228 (4): neither is a defect.**
- Connector configuration only holds free-text names that connector administrators type and can already read; the product never writes a record ID into them.
- No sequence of edits, permission changes or simultaneous saves lost or misplaced a hidden value.
- A user from another organization got 403 or 404 on all 312 operations that address the first organization's records, and nothing was saved.

This is an engineering review only. It grants no business approval (G1–G6), and product G6 never implies DG7.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-3/`:
- qa-verifier.json
- qa-verifier.verifications.json
- qa-verifier.md

Logs and scripts are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/round-3/`, and my probes in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/tests/round-3/`.
